focus: Review the variance definition if needed; focus today on explaining why a shift leaves variance unchanged.

sections.title: Objective and scope
paragraphs: Explain variance as expected squared distance from the mean, and use it on a finite distribution. Assume a real random variable with a finite second moment. This is synthetic acceptance-test material, not an independently sourced course handout.

sections.title: Definition and notation
paragraphs: Let $X$ be a real random variable and let $\mu=E[X]$. The variance is $\mathrm{Var}(X)=E[(X-\mu)^2]$. It has squared units; its square root has the same units as $X$.
The mean describes the centre. Squared distances prevent opposite signs from cancelling. Shifting every value and its mean by the same constant leaves those distances unchanged.

sections.title: A worked finite example
paragraphs: Suppose $X$ takes values 0 and 2, each with probability one half. Its mean is 1. Each squared distance from 1 equals 1, so its variance is 1. Adding 5 gives values 5 and 7 with mean 6 and the same variance.

For constants $a$ and $b$, linearity gives $E[aX+b]=a\mu+b$. Subtract this mean to get $a(X-\mu)$; square and average to obtain $\mathrm{Var}(aX+b)=a^2\mathrm{Var}(X)$. The case $a=0$ is a constant with zero variance.

sections.title: Independent practice
paragraphs: A different variable $Z$ takes values -2 and 4 with equal probability. Compute its mean and variance, then explain why adding a constant cannot change the variance. Try your reasoning before opening the solution appendix.

**Explain each step in your own words. Define the objects before using notation, state which assumptions you need, and check the constant case. A computed value alone does not establish general conceptual understanding. Ask for help when a step is unclear, and retain which hints you used. These sentences provide a deliberately long paragraph for testing safe pagination of formatted prose; they are not a learning assessment or a claim of educational effectiveness. The reader should preserve every word and all emphasis when dividing this paragraph across narrow pages.**

sections.title: Solution appendix
paragraphs: FIXTURE-SOLUTION: The mean of $Z$ is 1 and its variance is 9. Both distances from the mean have magnitude 3. For a shift, the mean moves by the same amount as each value, leaving every centred distance unchanged.
